title: Usage replay validation and quarantine for analytics backfills
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Provide a validation and quarantine layer for usage-event replays and historical backfills so we can run large-scale reprocessing with reduced risk of corrupting dashboards or billing metrics. This ticket implements a lightweight schema/semantic validator, a quarantine store for anomalous records, and a configurable dry-run path for canary replays.

Problem background:
- We've run multiple historical backfills where malformed or duplicated events slipped into downstream aggregations, causing billing mismatches and alert storms (see incident notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/analytics/backfill-incidents).
- Existing replay runners focus on throughput and resume tokens but lack pre-ingest validation and a safe quarantine flow.

Scope and proposal:
1) Validator component (streaming): run a fast, pluggable validation step before events are reinserted into main topics. Validations: JSON schema compatibility, timestamp monotonicity, event-size bounds, dedupe-token presence. Failures are classified as soft (fixable by transformation) or hard (reject).
2) Quarantine store (S3 + manifest): hard failures are written to a quarantine prefix with a manifest that records original offset, source-run id, and validation errors. Soft failures are optionally auto-transformed by configured mappers and retried.
3) Dry-run/canary mode: implement a replay mode that emits metrics to a shadow topic and to a dry-run dashboard without touching production aggregates. Canary supports sampling rate and model-based anomaly scoring.
4) Ops UI hooks: console links to view a quarantine batch, re-run with fixes, and approve releases to production ingestion. Minimal UI surface (link + run id) sufficient for MVP; follow-up PM ticket will expand UX.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Keep validator fast and stateless to avoid introducing throughput bottlenecks. We'll use a Rust microservice (aligned with serving runtime efforts) and instrument detailed histograms.
- Quarantine will be stored in compressed newline-delimited JSON on S3 (partitioned by day and run-id) to keep retrieval simple for analysts. This trades some storage cost for low operational complexity.
- Deduplication strategy: use incoming event dedupe-token when present; otherwise fall back to content-hash. This increases false-negative dedupe risk for extremely high-cardinality events but is acceptable for analytics backfill workloads.

Acceptance criteria:
- Validator processes a staging replay at 50k events/min without exceeding 20% additional latency on the replay pipeline.
- Quarantine manifests are queryable via the debugging endpoint and list at least the first 1000 failures for a run.
- Dry-run mode emits the same metrics as production ingestion to the dry-run dashboard and does not change production aggregates.
- Runbook and run-id metadata attached to every replay job.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/analytics-replay-validation (internal)
- Spike PR for validator binary: https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics/pull/4782
- Dry-run dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/dry-run-replay

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Validator bugs could produce false positives and cause mass quarantine. Mitigation: staged rollout (staging -> canary -> prod) and a reversible transform path for soft failures.
- Risk: Increased end-to-end latency for replays. Mitigation: run validator in parallel with current pipeline for a sampling of events first; if latency cost is unacceptable we will offload validation to an async pass and rely on quarantine remediation runs.

Next steps (short-term):
- Build rudimentary Rust validator that implements JSON schema + timestamp checks (owner: Ravi).
- Wire quarantine S3 layout and manifest format (owner: Data Infra).
- Add dry-run metric plumbing and Grafana panels (owner: Observability).
- Coordinate with PM for ops UI MVP scope (owner: Maya).
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting; agreed to prioritize schema + timestamp checks for MVP. Action: Ravi to prototype validator.

2026-02-20: Prototype validator binary completed (spike PR linked). Found that ~0.8% of historical events fail timestamp monotonicity in a 30-day sample. Decided to implement soft-fix that shifts timestamps to nearest valid boundary as a config option.
2026-02-28: Quarantine S3 layout draft reviewed with Data Infra — using run-id/day partitioning. Stored manifests will include original_topic and original_offset for traceability.
2026-03-05: Observability found that adding validator increased staging replay CPU by ~12%. Optimization plan: batch validation calls and reuse schema compilers between records.
2026-03-10: Integration test added for dry-run mode verifying no change to production aggregates; test currently passing against synthetic dataset. Preparing canary run on next weekend window.
2026-03-12: PM approved canary with 1% sampling for this weekend. QA checklist and runbook updated.

Dry-run emits metrics to dry-run dashboard and leaves production aggregates unchanged
Runbook written and sanity checks included for operator re-runs
